title: Infrastructure Health Checklist item C5 fails on main: 88 BLOCKER isolation violations make zig build test-env-verify exit 1 unconditionally
symptom: `zig build test-env-verify` exits 1 with `UNHEALTHY — 1 of 7 checks failed (C5)`. Checks C1, C2, C3, C4, C6, C7 all PASS; only C5 (test isolation lint) fails, reporting BLOCKER=88 MAJOR=6 across 127 integration test files (e.g. hardcoded UUIDs `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001` in adp04_user_tenant_binding_test.zig:38, tm01_tenant_list_test.zig:48, pd03_version_test.zig:112).
root_cause_analysis: The 88 BLOCKERs are hardcoded-UUID (T010) violations of INV-TI-2 that pre-date this branch. Confirmed pre-existing by running tools/lint_test_isolation.py against a clean origin/main worktree: identical result (BLOCKER=88 MAJOR=6, exit 1). The feature branch touches no files under tests/, and does not touch lint_test_isolation.py, its baseline, or verify_test_env.py — `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` over those paths is empty.
impact: CLAUDE.md instructs TEST-RUNNER to STOP and return FAIL with BLOCKER severity if any Infrastructure Health Checklist item fails, and docs/guides/test_infrastructure_guide.md §3 makes each item a hard gate. Because C5 fails unconditionally on main, that gate can never be satisfied as written — so every TEST-RUNNER either halts on an unrelated pre-existing condition or (worse) learns to run tests despite a red checklist. That is precisely the 'noise trains agents to ignore a checker' failure mode described in GH #469.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 88 T010 BLOCKERs is either fixed in the test source (per-test UUIDs) or deliberately baselined with a per-finding recorded reason
`zig build test-env-verify` exits 0 on a clean main
The baseline is NOT blanket-regenerated to silence findings (CLAUDE.md: never satisfy a gate by editing what it measures)
related: GH #469 / ISS-0152-prior covers baseline DRIFT (128 recorded vs 131 actual MAJORs) and explicitly notes BLOCKER=88 is identical on main and branch; this issue covers those 88 BLOCKERs themselves, which are what actually fail the C5 gate.
ISS-0171 / GH #498 / PR #499 - the fix that actually resolved this symptom (baseline line resync on 2026-08-06)
ISS-0181 / GH #512 - the residual debt this issue pointed at: 184 raw T010 hardcoded-UUID findings across 45 files, carried forward rather than written off

ISS-0180 / GH #511 - gate-integrity defect found while verifying this issue's premise: C3 migrates BPM_DB_URL while C4 verifies BPM_TEST_DB_URL, so C3 can report PASS against an unmigrated test database
GH #490 (8103072) - wired 55 previously-orphaned test files into build targets, raising the raw T010 count from 88 to 184 and shifting the lines that broke baseline suppression
notes: Not caused by the ISS-0148 fix. Filed per CLAUDE.md 'No Issue Left Local-Only' and 'Unblock-Everything'; it did not block measurement of the ISS-0148 primary criterion because C1-C4/C6/C7 passed and the DB baseline was verified sound (public-scope ledger 106 rows == 106 migration files, 0 ungranted locks). RESOLUTION NOTE (WF03-ISS-0152-20260807): closed as ALREADY_RESOLVED. The 88-BLOCKER premise was stale; the true raw count on current main is 184 across 45 files (225 findings total including 11 T020, 6 T030, 22 T050, 2 T060), all already recorded in the baseline and none newly escaping it. Full evidence in docs/issue-reports/ISS-0152-diagnosis.yaml.
resolution: ALREADY FIXED by ISS-0171 / PR #499 (2026-08-06) - the symptom is no longer reproducible on clean main. Verified on a pristine `git worktree` of main (HEAD b2cc55c), independent of the working tree so local edits could not influence the result: `tools/lint_test_isolation.py tests/integration` prints 'OK - 127 file(s) checked, no isolation issues. Suppressed 225 issue(s) from baseline' and exits 0. C5 invokes the linter WITHOUT --no-baseline, so the pre-existing findings are suppressed and the gate passes; the 88-BLOCKER figure in this issue corresponds to a --no-baseline run, a measurement the gate does not perform. GATE-GAMING AUDIT: because PR #499 regenerated a suppression file, it was audited rather than trusted - the baseline at 9a2b45c was diffed against its parent on the tuple (severity, code, file, message), deliberately ignoring `line`, since a pure line resync must not change the finding set. Result: 225 entries before, 225 after, 0 newly suppressed, 0 disappeared. issue_key() is 'severity|code|file|line|message', so the line shifts introduced by PR #490 had silently broken suppression; #499 restored the mapping without hiding anything new. Legitimate line resync, not gate-gaming. LOCAL EXIT 1 WAS ENVIRONMENT, NOT REPO, AND WAS A DIFFERENT CHECK (C4, not C5): (1) the process environment carried BPM_TEST_DB_URL on port 5434 (workspace 1's band), shadowing this workspace's 5453 - verify_test_env.py's documented precedence is 'real process environment always wins; .env fills gaps only' - so the check ran against the wrong database, one holding 96 leaked SCHEMA-mode fixture tenants versus 1 on the correct database; (2) two migrations (1136_iss0149_exp301_effects_outbox_tenant_scope.sql, 1137_iss0156_entity_instance_projection_backfill.sql) were unapplied locally. After correcting both, `zig build test-env-verify` reports 'HEALTHY - 7 checks passed', exit 0, with C1..C7 all PASS. NO CODE CHANGE WAS MADE AND NONE WAS NEEDED: git diff origin/main...HEAD over tools/lint_test_isolation.py, tools/lint_test_isolation.baseline.json, tools/verify_test_env.py and all of tests/ is EMPTY. No suppression was added, no linter rule weakened, no test deleted or skipped.
prevention: 1. Before filing a gate failure, run the gate exactly as the gate runs it. This issue reported a --no-baseline count against a gate that runs WITH the baseline; the two measure different things and only one of them is the gate. 2. Reproduce on a pristine worktree of main (`git worktree add <scratch> main`) before attributing a failure to the repository. Both causes of the exit 1 here were local: a shadowing process env var and unapplied migrations. In a multi-workspace checkout, always confirm which port band BPM_TEST_DB_URL actually resolves to - the process environment silently outranks .env. 3. When a fix regenerates a suppression baseline, audit it by diffing the finding set on (severity, code, file, message) with `line` excluded. That separates a legitimate line resync from a silent new suppression, and it is cheap. 4. A baseline is a debt ledger, not a fix. Closing this issue on 'the gate is green' without re-filing the 184 findings would have erased real debt; it is preserved as ISS-0181 / GH #512. 5. Line-keyed suppression is inherently fragile: any edit that shifts lines in a test file silently un-suppresses findings and forces a resync (the recurring cost ISS-0171 paid). Retiring the findings (ISS-0181) is the durable fix.
